I farm 10.1 mu, so I am not doing anything fancy. I will start from what has worked here in Quzhou and only push a little where I think the money can come back. On my wheat-maize land, I will keep 7 mu in the usual two-season rotation, because with well water that land is steadier and gives me grain every year. I will leave 3.1 mu for cotton in spring, because cotton still spreads my risk and I know how to manage it. I finished middle school, so I do look at cost, water, and fertilizer balance, not just copy blindly, but I still trust what I have seen in nearby fields. Wheat cannot go hungry early, so I will put enough base fertilizer and give 3 irrigations if water is normal. Maize is where I will not save too much nitrogen, because if maize turns pale after wheat harvest, yield drops fast and that loss hurts more than a little extra fertilizer cost. Cotton needs more watching than grain, especially insects, so I will not be stingy on sprays there. Labor in my house is limited, and some family work is off-farm, so I will keep tillage simple: rotary on the wheat ground, no-tillage or very light tillage for maize after wheat if I can move fast, and plough once for cotton ground. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and hold yield than save a few yuan and regret it at harvest.
